text: You'll hear three terms constantly in this field, often used loosely: Trailhead Playground, Developer Edition org, and sandbox. They're related, but they are not the same thing, and this lesson tells them apart for good.

A Trailhead Playground is a free Developer Edition org, created and managed through Trailhead specifically for learning. A Developer Edition org is that exact same org type, but signed up for directly at developer-dot-salesforce-dot-com, with no Trailhead badges or hands-on challenges attached to it. A sandbox is something else entirely — a copy of a company's own paid production org, used by real teams to build and test changes safely.

Here's the distinction that actually matters: where the data comes from. A Trailhead Playground and a Developer Edition org both start completely empty and belong to you alone. A sandbox always starts as a copy of one specific, real production org — it belongs to that company, not to you personally.

So which one is yours, right now? The Trailhead Playground you created in Lesson 3 — that's what you'll use for this entire course. Once you're actually working for a company as an admin, you'll be given a sandbox of their real production org to build and test in. The good news: Setup, Object Manager, and Flow look and work identically in all three, so everything you practice here transfers directly.
Three terms, told apart. Chapter One is done — next, Chapter Two: actually getting comfortable navigating the real Setup interface.
